SCIENCE PASSAGE 1: Enzyme Activity Across pH
Researchers measured the activity of an enzyme from two microorganisms across four buffer pH values. Equal enzyme concentrations and substrate amounts were used. Activity is reported as micromoles of product formed per minute.

According to the figure, what was the value for Microbe A enzyme at the x-axis value 6?
A) 2.1
B) 1.5
C) 3.2
D) 5.8
questions.explanation: Read the requested series at the specified x-value.

SCIENCE PASSAGE 3: Layered Thermal Insulation
A team wrapped identical warm-water containers with 0, 1, 2, or 3 felt layers. Experiment 1 measured water temperature after 30 minutes in still air. Experiment 2 repeated the test with a fan producing constant airflow. Every container began at 70°C and contained the same water volume.

According to the figure, what value was recorded for Still air at the x-axis value 1?
F) 48
G) 62
H) 54
J) 49
questions.explanation: Read the requested condition and series directly from the figure.

questions.stem:
SCIENCE PASSAGE 6: How Migrating Birds Recalibrate Direction
Three students discuss how migrating birds correct their direction after several cloudy days.

Student 1: Birds rely mainly on the position of the setting sun. A clear sunset after cloudy weather allows them to reset an internal compass for the next day.

Student 2: Birds rely mainly on Earth’s magnetic field. Cloud cover has little effect on the compass itself; errors arise when local magnetic conditions are disturbed.

Student 3: Birds use both cues. Magnetic information provides a continuous reference, while sunset information can recalibrate how that magnetic reference is interpreted at a particular location.

Which statement describes a point of agreement among the students?
A) They agree that only a laboratory instrument can create the phenomenon.
B) They agree that the phenomenon never changes with time.
C) They agree that all competing explanations have already been disproved.
D) All three students propose that birds possess directional information rather than simply following visible landmarks.

options.A: They agree that only a laboratory instrument can create the phenomenon.
options.B: They agree that the phenomenon never changes with time.
options.C: They agree that all competing explanations have already been disproved.
options.D: All three students propose that birds possess directional information rather than simply following visible landmarks.

questions.explanation: The stated point is consistent with every viewpoint.

SCIENCE MATERIAL SET 7
Students tested how water temperature affected the time required for a tablet to dissolve. They used identical tablets, 106 mL of water in each cup, and stirred each cup at the same rate.

TABLE 1
Temperature (°C) | Dissolving time (s)
10 | 30
20 | 22
30 | 17
40 | 13

Trial 2 repeated the procedure with twice the water volume. Researcher 1 claims that higher temperature increases particle motion and therefore decreases dissolving time. Researcher 2 agrees that temperature matters but claims that stirring rate is the dominant factor whenever stirring is not controlled.

Which unit is appropriate for the dependent variable?
A) degrees Celsius
B) seconds
C) milliliters
D) grams per liter
